identity.real_world_identity_notes: Le Mans-winning GT1 car with a carbon monocoque and a water-cooled 3.2 litre flat six derived from the 962. For 1998 Porsche fitted a new six-speed sequential gearbox to cut shift times, which matches the six gears and sequential lever seen in the cockpit.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
The clutch is required to move off, and the gear lever is a sequential stick rather than paddles.

In AMS2, no throttle lift is required on upshifts because a full-throttle clutchless upshift was accepted with automatic cut detected. No automatic blip was detected, so that implementation requires the driver to supply the downshift blip; the real car's blip technique remains unknown.

driver_summary: Six-speed sequential with a lever. The car cuts the upshift, so stay flat. Nothing blips the downshift, and whether this gearbox needs one to engage is not established, so blip anyway: it settles the car into the corner whether or not the box demands it.
